name: checkout-service
description: A small checkout service. Specs describe the module boundaries, the billing contract and the storage schema. The change sequence mixes three situations that a structural fingerprint can tell apart only poorly: a real contract break, a signature change with no semantic break, and a semantic break with no signature change.

specs.title: Checkout completes in one request
specs.statement: A customer can turn a cart into a paid order in a single round trip.
specs.boundary: Does not cover refunds or partial fulfilment.

specs.title: Three-layer service
specs.statement: Transport, domain and storage layers stay separate; the domain layer never imports the transport layer.

specs.title: Order record shape
specs.statement: The order record holds an id and the purchased items.

specs.title: Billing module contract
specs.statement: The billing module charges a cart total in a caller-supplied currency.
specs.boundary: Currency conversion lives outside this module.

specs.title: Auth module boundary
specs.statement: Session handling stays inside the auth module.

specs.title: Notification delivery contract
specs.statement: Order notifications are delivered before checkout returns.

specs.title: Audit trail
specs.statement: Every order mutation is recorded with its prior value.

specs.title: Add coupon support to billing
specs.statement: A coupon reduces the charged total by a fixed amount.

steps.label: session-token
steps.note: A real contract break: callers must now pass a token.

tasks.question: How is a Session constructed?
tasks.answer_valid: Session(user) opens a session for that user.
tasks.answer_stale: Session(user, token, ttl) now requires an explicit token.

steps.label: charge-currency-default
steps.note: Signature changed, meaning did not: every caller passes a currency explicitly.

tasks.question: Which currency does charge default to?
tasks.answer_valid: charge defaults to USD; callers pass the currency anyway.

steps.label: notify-async
steps.note: Meaning changed, signature did not: delivery became asynchronous. Invisible to a structure diff.

tasks.question: Is a notification delivered before checkout returns?
tasks.answer_valid: Yes, delivery happens before checkout returns.
tasks.answer_stale: No, the notification is queued and delivered asynchronously.

steps.label: order-fields
steps.note: A record shape change that really does reach its dependents.

tasks.question: Which fields does an Order record hold?
tasks.answer_valid: An Order holds an id and its items.
tasks.answer_stale: An Order also holds a currency field.

steps.label: coupon-optional-param
steps.note: A backward-compatible optional parameter. Structure moves, meaning does not.

tasks.question: What does apply_coupon take?
tasks.answer_valid: apply_coupon takes a code and an amount.
tasks.answer_stale: apply_coupon also accepts a stackable flag.

steps.label: coupon-body-tidy
steps.note: Body-only edit. Neither a structure diff nor a validity change.
